answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cost cut; the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, so renewing or negotiating terms cannot meet the target. Memory c2 records that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor last year cut unit cost sharply, with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—directly relevant to whether a switch can deliver the required savings without introducing delivery risk. Memory c4 confirms the incumbent only moved under benchmarking pressure, which is unavailable now. Switching primary vendor is the single action that addresses the cost mandate within the 14-day expiry window. The 94% assembly-line utilization with no buffer is the key risk: a botched transition could halt deliveries. Mitigation: run the new vendor's first shipments in parallel with the incumbent's final deliveries over the 14-day overlap, and keep the incumbent on a short month-to-month bridge (precedent in memory c5) only if the switchover slips. Deferring is not viable—the contract does not auto-renew. Adding a second source or renegotiating terms does not close the 18% gap this cycle.
